en.title: Balkans snow in the last days: which country got the most? Slovenia, Croatia, Serbia, Montenegro and Bulgaria compared
en.description: From 13 to 19 November 2026 Slovenia got the most snow and kept it; Serbia and Croatia had a deep but short white weekend; Montenegro only on Durmitor; Bulgaria almost none. The ranking, with links to each country report.
en.lede: Five countries, one week, very different luck. Between Friday 13 and Thursday 19 November 2026 a cold spell brought the first real snow of the season to the western Balkans, then milder air took most of it away. Slovenia comes out clearly on top: it had the most new snow, it is snowing again today, and 14 of its 19 higher ski areas are white. Bulgaria comes last. Here is the full comparison, country by country.

p: Slovenia got the most, and is the only one of the five with real snow on the slopes today: 28 cm on the upper slopes of Kanin, 20 cm at Kranjska Gora, 16 cm on Vogel. Montenegro comes second today, with 6 cm left on Savin Kuk above Žabljak. Bulgaria has 2 cm at the top of Borovets and Bansko. Croatia and Serbia, which had deep snow last weekend, are bare again.

If you rank by the deepest snow reached at any point this week, the order changes: Serbia's Tornik on Zlatibor reached 39 cm on Sunday 15 November, Slovenia's Gače 38 cm on Saturday 14 November and Croatia's Rudnik Tršće 29 cm the same day. Those were short peaks on modest mountains, and none of them survived to Wednesday.

sections.h: Slovenia: the most snow, and the only fresh snow
p: Slovenia had two snowfalls in a week: Friday 13 November, which left 30 cm on Vogel and 19 cm on Rogla by Saturday, and today, Thursday 19 November, with about 37 cm of new snow on Kanin, 21 cm on Krvavec and 18 cm on Pokljuka. Over the week, Kanin's upper slopes collected about 44 cm, the most anywhere in the five countries.

The high weather station on Kredarica, below Triglav at 2,515 m, measured 30 cm every morning since 14 November. More snow is due on Sunday 22 November in the Julian Alps. Full details are in our Slovenia report, linked below.

sections.h: Croatia and Serbia: a white weekend, then nothing
p: Croatia's snow fell almost all on Friday 13 November: about 30 cm on the upper slopes of northern Velebit, 29 cm on Bjelolasica, 19 cm on Platak. The weather station at Zavižan, at 1,597 m, had 16 cm on Saturday and Sunday and bare ground on Tuesday 17 November. Today no Croatian ski area has snow (see the Croatia report below).

Serbia followed the same script further east. Tornik had 34 cm on Saturday and 39 cm on Sunday, the station in Zlatibor town measured 11 cm, and all of it was gone by Wednesday 18 November. Kopaonik, high as it is, only got about 2 cm (Serbia report below).

Montenegro's snow came in small daily doses, and only Durmitor kept it: Savin Kuk collected about 22 cm over the week and still has 6 cm, while Kolašin 1600 and 1450 on Bjelasica are bare (Montenegro report below).

Bulgaria was mostly outside the storm. Borovets and Bansko each picked up about 12 cm in small falls, but neither ever held more than 4 cm on the ground, and Pamporovo and Vitosha are bare (Bulgaria report below).

sections.h: Bosnia and Herzegovina, the missing neighbour
p: Bosnia and Herzegovina sits right in the middle of this map and had a week much like Croatia's: some snow on the high mountains last weekend, bare slopes now, and snow forecast for later next week. It has its own report today, linked below.
Taken together, the region's snow this week was a preview. The places that kept it are the highest ones: the Julian Alps on Kanin and Vogel, and Durmitor, where Savin Kuk climbs to 2,175 m.

sections.h: What comes next, country by country
p: Slovenia gets the next real snow, on Sunday 22 November: 7 to 13 cm on the upper slopes of Kranjska Gora, about 10 cm in the middle forecast. Croatia and Montenegro have their best chance on Monday 23 November, with a few centimetres: Bjelolasica 7 cm and Savin Kuk 3 cm in the middle forecast. Bulgaria's one chance is the same Monday, 3 cm in the middle forecast for Borovets but up to 12 cm in the highest.

Serbia is the driest: the middle forecast gives about 1 cm on Kopaonik for the whole week to 26 November. For a ski trip in the next ten days, the Julian Alps are the only safe bet for natural snow; everywhere else, wait for December and follow each resort's own opening news.

advice: Most snow this week, and the only fresh snow today: Slovenia's Julian Alps (Kanin, Kranjska Gora, Vogel).
Croatia's and Serbia's white weekend melted by Wednesday 18 November.
Next snow: Sunday 22 November in Slovenia, Monday 23 November elsewhere, mostly a few centimetres.
